issues.description: Method name inconsistency for the operation that computes a meal's total price: the problem statement UML declares a static method calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int (problem_statement.md, UML line 29) and the text also refers to calculateTotalPrice as the required static method (problem_statement.md, line 80). In the template repository Main.java the example call uses shop.computeMealCost(...) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, line 13). In the solution, SealSaloon defines public static int computeMealCost(Meal) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java, line 57) but the solution's Main.java calls shop.calculateTotalPrice(...) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, line 13). This creates a cross-artifact naming mismatch (problem statement vs. template vs. solution implementation and solution example call) that can confuse students and will cause compilation or test failures if instructors/tests expect one name but the code provides another.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred): rename the implementation method computeMealCost(Meal) to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) in SealSaloon.java and update any calls (template and solution Main.java) to shop.calculateTotalPrice(...). Also update the method name in any tests or examples. Option B: alternatively, update the problem statement UML and text to require computeMealCost(Meal) and adjust all example code to call computeMealCost. Ensure the final chosen name is used consistently in the problem statement, UML, template examples, solution implementation, and tests.
